question.text: 'Chola Cat II AIF' has a committed corpus of INR 600 crore. The drawdown schedule is: Year 1 = 40%, Year 2 = 30%, Year 3 = 20%, balance at discretion. By the end of Year 2, what is the TOTAL called capital (fund-level)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Cumulative through Year 2 = 40% + 30% = 70%. 70% x INR 600 cr = INR 420 crore. The Trap: Option A is Year 1 only. Option B is Year 2 alone. Option D is 90% (adds Y3 erroneously). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C all test multi-year drawdown schedules — a staple. Manager's Pro-Tip: Match your drawdown schedule to actual deployment velocity rather than a formulaic linear call. LPs value capital-efficiency (higher IRR on called capital) over a predictable but premature call schedule.
